plain_english: This record concerns John Glasgow, a sailor in Saltcoats within Ardrossan parish, who died in December 1636. It is explicitly headed testament dative: an estate administration rather than a freshly recovered personal will.

Isobell Gray is expressly his widow. The opening continuation names Katherine and Agnes as his lawful children and calls the deceased their father. The concluding caution repeats the daughters' names and their relationship to the Saltcoats sailor. The record does not expressly make Isobell their mother.

John Broune/Brown, also a sailor in Saltcoats, appears in the final caution. That administrative role does not prove that he was a relative. The inventory and accounts are faint; detailed equipment readings and money totals have not been silently reconstructed.

The documented widow, children, occupation and locality distinguish this household from the known Glasgow-1030/Jonet Mathie family. No new bridge joins the households, so Glasgow-1030 remains excluded as the present identification. No daughter Mary is established by the family clauses.
findings: Page 478, opening: 'Testament dative', sailor occupation, Saltcoats, Ardrossan parish and widow Isobell Gray are visible together.
Page 479, first lines: Katherine and Agnes are called lawful children and the deceased is called their father. This is direct paternal evidence, not a conclusion drawn merely from executorship.

Page 480, first paragraph: the caution repeats 'lawfull bairnes of umqle Johne glasgow sailler in Saltcoittis', corroborating the household identification within the same record, not as an independent source.
Nothing freshly read establishes Isobell's maternity, names Mary as a daughter, or connects the sailor to Jonet Mathie and John Glasgow-1030.

The entry begins at the foot of page 478 and ends in the upper part of page 480. The surrounding estates are excluded. All three supplied pages were examined, but the accounts are incompletely transcribed.
